items.review_rationale: Read second boundary characterization through intersections of closures of A and complement in X, distinguishing both closure operations from arbitrary complementary subsets.

references.context: Elements in fixed ambient X not in A, whose closure is taken in X.
Points adhering simultaneously to A and its ambient complement.

references.disposition: Both formulas represent same boundary because complement of interior A is closure of complement.

items.review_rationale: Read closure of subset as intersection of all closed supersets within given topological space, with closedness via open complement.

references.context: Subset F whose complement relative to X belongs to tau.

references.phrase: intersection of all closed supersets of A
references.context: Set of points lying in every closed subset F of X that contains A.

references.disposition: The intersection remains closed and contains A; no arbitrary extrinsic universe is used.

items.review_rationale: Read order-theoretic least closed superset characterization of topological closure, specifying inclusion relation among closed supersets.

references.phrase: family of closed supersets of A
references.context: All F⊆X with A⊆F and X\F open.
Unique closed C containing A such that C⊆F for every closed F containing A.

references.disposition: Closure is contained in each closed superset, not merely one of many minimal elements.

items.review_rationale: Read linearity of map between vector spaces over common field through preservation of affine combination T(av+w)=aT(v)+T(w), ensuring same module scalar field.

references.phrase: vector spaces V,W over common field K

references.context: For each scalar a∈K and vectors v,w∈V, T(av+w)=aT(v)+T(w).

references.phrase: same scalar field in source and target
references.disposition: Linearity uses one common K-action on both spaces; not merely an additive set mapping.
